summary: The note describes Cirque Calder, an artistic rendering of a circus created by American artist Alexander Calder. It consists of wire models, typically made of wire and wood, rigged to perform the functions of circus performers such as contortionists, sword eaters and lion tamers. Calder began improvising performances of this circus while living in Paris, commenting in French during the shows.
one_line: Cirque Calder is Alexander Calder's miniature circus of wire and wood performers he improvised in Paris.
key_facts: Cirque Calder is an artistic rendering of a circus created by the American artist Alexander Calder.
The Cirque Calder models are rigged with wire so they can perform the functions of the circus performers they represent.
The performers represented include contortionists, sword eaters and lion tamers.
The models of Cirque Calder are made of various items, generally wire and wood.
Alexander Calder began improvising performances of Cirque Calder during his time in Paris.
Alexander Calder would comment in French during his Cirque Calder performances.
